summary: Reliability release: strict name resolution and module isolation, function-value marshalling, safer install paths, and numeric narrowing for float vector stores.

highlights.title: Stricter name resolution and imports
highlights.text: A bare call now binds the calling module's own definition, including private helpers, so a same-named function elsewhere can no longer hijack it, the defect class behind a startup crash in a service harness. Private constants stay private, and an unresolved import is one clear error instead of a silent phantom.

highlights.title: Function values survive every boundary
highlights.text: Function-typed values marshal correctly through C calls, struct fields, locals and vector elements: callbacks re-pass cleanly, element calls of any arity return their declared type, and module-scope function pointers can be called and reassigned.

highlights.title: Safer installs and one packages home
highlights.text: Install commands refuse mangled or relative home paths with a clear error instead of scattering directories, archive extraction is deterministic, and when several home candidates exist the compiler picks the one that actually holds installed packages.

highlights.title: Float vector stores convert their values
highlights.text: Writing a literal into a float vector element now converts it to the element type: 7.0 into a Float32 slot stores 7 rather than zero, and integer literals convert numerically instead of being reinterpreted as bit patterns.

highlights.title: JSON and string byte paths go linear
highlights.text: Parsing large JSON documents is now linear: the parser reads the raw UTF-8 bytes once instead of rescanning the string per character, and the string slice and byte-copy helpers do the same. Large numeric payloads parse in well under a second, and the Unicode-escape defect that dropped the byte after an escape is fixed.

highlights.title: Contracts and coverage across the standard library
highlights.text: Coverage waves since the last release added clauses across math, collections, crypto, os, hash, sync and more, lifting public-function coverage from the low sixties to nearly seventy percent. The sync, crypto and hash surfaces are now almost fully covered, and every wave is locked by dedicated probes.

known_issues: Comparing containers with equality operators is pointer identity: two equal vectors compare unequal, and equal results containing vectors compare unequal; deep container equality is queued.
A confined allocation followed by a free can spin in the guard heap; keep the exit block as the last statement and avoid manual free until the runtime patch lands.
